idiom_name: module tree with `pub use` re-exports (facade crate); private-field service struct when state is injected
implementation_notes: Rust facades are module boundaries: keep subsystem modules private or pub(crate), and expose a curated set through pub use in lib.rs so downstream crates only ever see the intended paths - RFC 40 even describes the standard library itself as 'a facade in front of component libraries'. When the facade needs configuration or injected collaborators, expose a struct with private fields and methods (ReportService::generate_from_file); std::fs is the stdlib precedent of a uniform facade over platform-specific calls.
pitfalls: `pub use` of an item from a private module is fine, but declaring a whole `pub mod` re-exports its entire tree; audit what is reachable from the crate root.
Returning subsystem error types in facade signatures couples callers to internals; define a small public error enum and convert with From/?.
Public struct fields let callers bypass invariants; keep facade state private and expose methods.
Generic trait bounds in the facade's public API leak implementation choices; prefer concrete collaborators or a small facade-owned trait.
